solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: City in East Asia backs political party, overwhelmed by rage

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed by it, so the rage word swallows the other pieces

parts.note: a rage is a craze or passing fashion, a fad

indicators.note: backs, as a verb, says the continent's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written
Lab is the short form of Labour, the British political party

explanation.surface: A city in East Asia turns on a political party in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only 'City in East': Faisalabad is in Pakistan, so 'Asia' belongs to the wordplay, and 'backs' is a verb meaning reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Faisalabad is a large industrial city in Pakistan's Punjab, an Eastern city in the broad sense of 'the East' as Asia.

clue.text: A bouquet not all there — am I suffering from this?

definitions.text: A bouquet not all there — am I suffering from this?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not all there says the word is missing a letter, here its last

parts.note: a wine's nose is its bouquet or aroma

indicators.note: suffering suggests something in a bad way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they have lost the sense of smell because a wine's aroma seems faint.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSE loses its E to give NOS, and 'suffering' rearranges AM I to MIA. Read whole, the clue describes the condition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Anosmia is the loss of the sense of smell, so a wine's aroma would seem partly missing.

clue.text: United supporters turned up in confusion

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
fans are supporters of a team

explanation.surface: Manchester United's fans arrive in a state of disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAFU began as US military slang for a chaotic mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a chaotic mix-up or muddle, a state of confusion.

clue.text: Of late, Times cryptic really absorbs

indicators.note: absorbs says the shuffled letters take the other piece inside them
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: TT stands for times, multiplication written twice in short as x x, read as T T

explanation.surface: Lately the Times cryptic has become really engrossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges REALLY to LAERLY, and 'absorbs' takes TT into it. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Latterly means recently or in recent times, of late.

clue.text: Chap wearing motley sports blues and greens

indicators.note: wearing says the shuffled letters are put on around the man's name
motley means varied and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Russ is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man dressed in a colourful mix of sporting blues and greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greens' is the definition, though after 'blues' it reads like another colour; 'motley' is the anagram signal and 'wearing' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels sprouts are green vegetables, and greens is a general word for leafy vegetables.

clue.text: One acre needed to support pea plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so this follows the pea word

parts.note: dahl (dal, dhal) is a split pea or lentil
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gardener needs an acre of ground to hold up a pea plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden plant grown for its showy flowers, named after the botanist Dahl.

clue.text: Blow your nose!

definitions.meaning: a punch or knock, especially to the head
a slang word for the nose, the thing on your face

explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang senses of one word: a blow on the head, and the nose itself.

clue.text: Deprecates monarch, getting month away in cooler?

indicators.note: month away means the abbreviation for month is taken out

parts.note: to deprecate is to express disapproval of, to condemn
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone disapproving of the king is sent away for a month to the cooler, prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like slang for prison, but a condenser cools vapour into liquid. CONDEMNS minus M gives CONDENS, then ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A condenser is a device that cools a gas or vapour so that it turns into liquid.

clue.text: Close match for garment

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a cup match between two teams

explanation.surface: A close game played for a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie is the British term for a knockout fixture, as in an FA Cup tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment worn in bed.

clue.text: Artist's work always getting rejected

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: to go is to function or work, as a machine goes

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the word for always is read in reverse

parts.note: ay (also aye) is an old and dialect word for always

explanation.surface: A painter's output is always being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: AY meaning 'ever, always' is an old word still met in crosswords; 'work' as the verb go, as in 'the engine won't go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter of the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

clue.text: What healer may do when in a rush? That's risky

definitions.text: What healer may do when in a rush?
definitions.meaning: a healer in a hurry might lay on hands and then leave, a touch followed by a quick departure
a ... situation is precarious, with the outcome uncertain

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a precarious situation whose outcome could go either way, which is what risky means.

clue.text: Place in Middle East will succeed I reckon

indicators.note: to succeed is to follow after, so this group comes after the single letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says the verb for place goes inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a spot in the Middle East will do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun but is the verb put; 'succeed' means follow, not thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to attribute or ascribe, to reckon something as belonging to someone.

clue.text: Knife fight takes place around time I left

indicators.note: around says the fight word goes about the other letters

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or brief quarrel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knife fight breaks out somewhere at the moment someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes place' looks like a single phrase meaning happens, but 'place' and 'takes' are only link words; the container signal is 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a thin tapering blade.

clue.text: Unable to meet standard, female's sent back by lecturer at first

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in 'up to par'

indicators.note: sent back says the woman's name is written in reverse

parts.note: Ella is a woman's name; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A woman who falls short of the required standard is returned by her tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to meet standard' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'meet': parallel lines never meet. 'by' is a link joining the lecturer's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel lines run side by side at a constant distance and so can never meet.

clue.text: Academician shrank at raunchy material

parts.note: A is a dictionary abbreviation for academician

indicators.note: raunchy suggests wild and unruly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic flinched at some vulgar material.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a fabric of curly lamb's fleece or a cloth made to imitate it.

clue.text: Sick son needs a seat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
a pew is a bench seat in a church

explanation.surface: A boy who feels ill needs to sit down.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, to be sick, here as a verb.

clue.text: He perhaps has run away from arresting criminal

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged
away from says the letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A man has fled from a policeman detaining a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man but is the chemical symbol for helium. ARRESTING loses an R to give ARESTING, and 'criminal' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, symbol He, is one of the noble gases, so it is an example of the class.

clue.text: Osteopath regularly visited clan

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the word is taken, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A bone doctor made regular calls on a family group.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a division of a clan, especially in Ireland or Scotland, and so stands for a clan or family group.

clue.text: You will keep girl back after end of lecture? It's not fair

indicators.note: after says the next group follows the single letter
end of says only the final letter of the word is used
will keep means holds inside, so the old pronoun contains the girl

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: back says the girl's name is written in reverse

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A student complains that a girl was kept behind after a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' means beautiful here, not just, so the complaint is about looks; 'back' and 'will keep' do the turning and the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, the opposite of fair in its old sense of beautiful.

clue.text: Pattern of actions showing ecclesiastical council's out of love with Catholic Church

indicators.note: out of love means without the letter that stands for love, so it is removed

parts.note: a synod is a church council; the 's means 'is'
O is love, the zero score in tennis
Rome is shorthand for the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: A church council has fallen out with the Catholic Church, revealing a pattern of behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of love' reads as falling out of affection, but it is a deletion: SYNOD loses its O to become SYND.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a characteristic set of symptoms or behaviours that occur together, a recognisable pattern.

clue.text: Cost of anchoring boats creating anger in Cowes, we're told?

parts.note: Cowes, a sailing town on the Isle of Wight, said aloud is cows, whose call is moo
rage is extreme anger

explanation.surface: Mooring fees for yachts are causing fury in Cowes.
explanation.walkthrough: COWES, on the Isle of Wight, is the home of British yachting, which makes the boating surface apt. 'anger in cows' is moo-rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the charge made for mooring a boat, a fee for anchoring.

clue.text: Bump start for Jag (that's a Jaguar)

indicators.note: start for means the first letter of the word

parts.note: an ounce is a big cat, the snow leopard, a name also loosely used for the jaguar

explanation.surface: A Jag car is bumped into life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bump start' reads as a way to start a car, but splits: 'Bump' is the definition and 'start for' picks J.
explanation.definitionFit: To jounce is to bump or jolt up and down.

clue.text: Beat black and blue, or get beaten around the head in assault?

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go about the single letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: beaten here means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the head is the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone beaten black and blue during an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black and blue' looks like the result of a beating but is fodder, with 'and' only a joiner; 'the head in assault' gives just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour is to beat or thrash someone soundly, and figuratively to overdo an argument.

clue.text: Somewhat flustered hotelier gets highly emotional

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hotel manager in a flap becomes very worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot means burning with passion or excitement, so it describes someone highly emotional.

clue.text: Pet bites bishop so gets shut out

indicators.note: bites says the pet word closes around the letter, as teeth close on something

parts.note: dear and pet are both terms of endearment
B is the abbreviation for bishop, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A dog bites a bishop and is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to exclude or bar someone, to shut them out.

clue.text: Food and drink from the east is found around the Scandinavian city

indicators.note: around says the reversed food-and-drink pair goes about the next word
read from the east is read right to left in an across clue

parts.note: grub is slang for food
nog is a drink, such as eggnog or a strong ale
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food and drink from the East are on offer around a Swedish city.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'from the east' means read right to left; nog is an old word for strong beer or eggnog.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothenburg is Sweden's second city, a port on the west coast of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Scholar's written about middle part of Pride and Prejudice

indicators.note: written about says the scholar's letters are placed around the next piece

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar; the 's adds S

indicators.note: middle part means the centre letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An academic has written about the heart of a famous Jane Austen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride and Prejudice' looks like the title of the novel, but it splits: 'Pride' gives its middle letter I and 'Prejudice' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a one-sided inclination or partiality, which is what a prejudice is.

clue.text: Woman in short trousers

indicators.note: short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: jeans are denim trousers

explanation.surface: A woman dressed in shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a woman's first name.

clue.text: English eccentric, say, acquires second plane? To a T, this describe his financial situation

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a plane is a tree, the plane tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric Englishman buys a second aeroplane, which shows how well off he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft but is the tree; 'To a T' just brings in the final letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on easy street means living in financial comfort, free of money worries.
